answer: Proof-of-Stake acts as a bridge between capital and network authority, requiring agents to lock tokens in a secure vault to participate in consensus. Unlike the hollow weight of a walnut, which implies fragility, this mechanism imposes a rigorous economic cost: an attacker must acquire a majority of total stake to spoof identities. By tying voting power directly to locked collateral rather than node count, the system renders the creation of cheap, fake identities financially prohibitive and ultimately futile.
